threads.body: [Style] Class members should be ordered as static fields, static initializers, then instance fields. Move this static queue (and its initializer block) ahead of `isSecurityManagerSupportEnabled`.

replies.body: good point, i applied the suggestion. i was even thinking about a generic wrapper for such cases, but since the implementation is simple and this case shouldn't appear often in the code i didn't want to introduce additional complexity

threads.body: [General] This warning cannot fire for the realistic failure. `RemappingUrlStreamHandler` opens the jar while building the URL, so a truncated or non-zip extension jar throws `IllegalStateException`, not `MalformedURLException`. It escapes `createExtensionClassLoader()`, which runs before the `try` in `AgentStarterImpl.start()`, so startup aborts, none of these deferred messages are flushed, and the remaining configured locations are never checked. Could we handle the jar-open failure here too?

replies.body: changed handling to `IOException`, this will mean we are now failing-safe in case of issues with loading a JAR, but i agree it's a better solution

threads.body: [General] In the shipped shaded agent, an existing `.jar` that `JarFile` cannot open makes `addFileUrl` log the specific failure and return `false`, so this block then contradicts it with the generic "does not exist, is not a jar file" warning. The same happens when every candidate jar in a directory fails. Could we track whether a candidate jar was found separately from whether it loaded, and warn here only when none was found?

replies.body: sure, separated found and loaded logs :)

threads.body: [Style] Dropping the `System.err` call from `addFileUrl` leaves `includeEmbeddedExtensionsIfFound` as the only member that needs this suppression. Move `@SuppressWarnings("SystemOut")` from the class onto that method (line 99), the way `AgentStarterImpl` and `NoopLoggingCustomizer` do.

replies.body: moved to method-level, also, do you think migrating `System.err` usages in `includeEmbeddedExtensionsIfFound` to the new logging way is a good idea? we could fully unify the logging in this class
I think the current split makes sense: defer routine discovery logs so they respect the configured logger and debug level, but keep failures that could prevent logging initialization on `System.err`

threads.body: [General] `addFileUrl` now returns a boolean that no caller reads, since `parseLocation` tracks `found` on its own. Restore the `void` return type and drop the value returns (lines 212 and 215).
I think ideally the logger should buffer the messages until the logging system is initialized, but this is fine too.
